subject.title: Slack: Include file attachment metadata in inbound message delivery to agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared cross-channel inbound attachment metadata contract for agents, or keep Slack file details limited to placeholders, media paths, and download-file?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the durable fix changes the agent-facing channel/plugin context API rather than only Slack internals.

options.title: Add shared attachment metadata
options.body: Introduce a channel-agnostic metadata block and populate Slack file id, name, MIME type, and size while preserving current media fields.

options.title: Keep current Slack surfaces
options.body: Continue relying on placeholders, media paths/types, and download-file, then close or defer structured metadata.

options.title: Add Slack-only metadata
options.body: Ship a narrow Slack-only field now, accepting future cross-channel cleanup risk if other transports need the same contract.

recommendation.title: Add shared attachment metadata
recommendation.body: Introduce a channel-agnostic metadata block and populate Slack file id, name, MIME type, and size while preserving current media fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice extends the shared channel turn media facts and Slack inbound file URL surfaces recently shaped by this owner.
